source: Cambodia Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), "ប្រព័ន្ធវប្បកម្មដំណាំស្រូវ តាមគោលការណ៍ធម្មជាតិ (ប.វ.ស)" [System of Rice Intensification Following Natural Principles / SRI], 14-page Khmer-language handout/booklet, undated, no author or elibrary URL visible on any page (footer reads "កំរណ៉ការអភិវ័ទ្ធន៍វិស្ស័យកសិកម្ម ខែត្តកំពងចាម" = "Agricultural Extension/Skills Development Office, Kampong Cham province")
text:
Water management under SRI (per the source document): irrigate the field carefully, but avoid keeping deep standing water while rice is actively growing (vegetative stage), since this is said to restrict root development. Remove weeds thoroughly from the field, because weeds compete strongly with rice for fertilizer, water, and soil nutrients. Where feasible, dig a small farm pond of about 20 m x 20 m to provide irrigation water during dry spells and which can additionally be used for fish raising. After transplanting, maintain a shallow water level in the field of no more than about 2-3 cm, or alternate between a shallow water layer and just keeping the soil moist.

A caution noted in the source: transplanted seedlings can be damaged/die if the field is kept with too much water immediately after transplanting. Water should instead be carefully maintained through the reproductive stage (from booting/heading through the milk/soft-dough grain-filling stage), when adequate water becomes more important.

Weeding and top-dressing: weed the field thoroughly and follow with an application of additional (top-dress) fertilizer, especially well-decomposed compost, timed to coincide with the rice tillering stage. A second round of weeding and top-dressing is done again at the panicle-initiation stage, to help the rice develop long, strong panicles.
